column1: # What each gating guard reads, and the job that must therefore run it (#1514).
# `.pi/guards.tsv` says *whether* a guard gates. This file says *what it reads*, so the path→subject
# map in `.github/ci-affected.tsv` can be compared with the guards instead of trusted. The defect it
# closes has now happened twice: `engine/.pi/**` did not reach `audit` (#1498), and `docs/**` did not
# either — so a pull request that rewrote seven specification documents reported success without
# running the validator whose subject is documentation (#1514).
#   guard    the guard script, as `.pi/guards.tsv` names it
#   reads    a path glob whose contents the guard reads
#   why      what the content of those paths is to that guard
#   1. `reads` must match at least one tracked path — a glob nobody's file matches is a row that
#   2. the map must route `reads` to `audit`, the job that runs `validate-guards.sh`, which runs
#   3. every `run_here=yes` guard in `.pi/guards.tsv` must appear here at least once, so a new
#      guard cannot be added without saying what it reads.
# The cost of rule 2 is stated rather than hidden: `audit` is selected by the rows whose contents a
# guard reads, so it runs on more changes than it used to. That is the price of the guard running at
# all; the alternative is the green pipeline this issue was filed about.
